key_insight: QuASAR uses two LLM agents to turn literature-derived scientific computations into runnable quantum prototypes, enabling exploration rather than demonstrating quantum advantage.
engineering_relevance: The framework could help scientific computing teams screen quantum-algorithm opportunities and benchmark prototypes before committing specialist effort.
method: Screen scientific literature for computational kernels with plausible quantum analogues and supporting citations.
Independently verify citations, reconstruct computational structure, and formulate quantum mappings.
Build and execute prototypes, then benchmark against classical baselines.
evidence_signal: Of ten astrophysics-derived candidates, nine reached small-scale benchmarked prototypes; three detailed case studies covered combinatorial optimization, stochastic simulation, and Bayesian inference.
watch_item: None of the three detailed cases achieved quantum advantage at tested scales, and their astrophysical framing still requires expert validation.
paper_title: QuASAR: Toward an LLM-Assisted Framework for Screening, Prototyping, and Assessing Quantum-Advantage Opportunities in Scientific Computing
